gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Sun Gold Power's SPH6548P, a 6.5 kW 48 V split-phase inverter charger with two built-in MPPT solar controllers, costs $1,035 at sungoldpower.com today. That is $465 less than EG4's 6000XP at Signature Solar ($1,499.99), $521 less than the $1,556 6000XP card ChatGPT showed, and works out to about $159 per kW against $250 per kW for the 6000XP.
standout_why: I compared against four sets of pages. Two are cited rivals: currentconnected.com/eg4-inverters prices only EG4 models (6000XP $1,449.99 and 12000XP $2,099.99, both out of stock) and ecosolarkits.com/blogs/guides/eg4-vs-sol-ark prices only EG4 and Sol-Ark. The third is the cited EG4 12000XP maker page, which shows no price. The fourth is two top results that print no prices at all: wildjoule.com/best-hybrid-inverter names a SunGoldPower 10 kW unit but gives no price or solar input, and signaturesolarsolutions.com/eg4-inverters-compared lists idle draw but no prices. None of these pages prices a Sun Gold Power all-in-one or works out price per kW for the off-grid units. Idle draw is already covered by signaturesolarsolutions (6000XP 50 W, 12000XP 70 W, FlexBOSS21 65 W), so it is not a gap.
decides: This confirms ChatGPT's grouping but undercuts its 'best value' pick. For a budget off-grid 120/240 V all-in-one, the SPH6548P costs $415 to $521 less than the 6000XP and gives 0.5 kW more rated output. Neither unit sells power back to the grid; the SPH6548P listing says 'UL 1741 by ETL for Off Grid Solar System'. Sun Gold Power's 10 kW all-in-one at $1,422 costs less than the 6000XP and is about $678 cheaper than the 12000XP ($2,099.99, out of stock at Current Connected). For grid export, the FlexBOSS21 ($3,599.99, 10-year warranty) is still the value pick over the Sol-Ark 15K ($5,650). The SPH6548P stays a 'consider' rather than a winner because I could not source its total solar input in watts, its idle draw, or its warranty. Our Sun Gold Power 6000W low-frequency inverter charger should not be used for this question: its listing describes only an inverter, a battery charger and an AC transfer switch, with no solar controller.
